subtopics.title: How Costs Behave When Output Moves

questions.question: Variable costs are:
options: Constant per unit but growing in total as output grows
Constant in total at any output

questions.question: Fixed costs of R658 000 at an output of 10 000 pairs work out per pair to:
options: R65,80 — and the per-unit figure shrinks as output spreads the fixed total

questions.question: Kagiso's total variable cost of R48 per pair consists of:
options: Materials R23, labour R17, factory rent R8
Materials R23, labour R17, depreciation R8
Direct materials R23, direct labour R17, and selling and distribution R8

questions.question: A unit cost that includes fixed costs is only true:
options: At the specific output it was computed for — fixed cost per unit changes with volume

questions.question: Contribution per unit is calculated as:
options: Selling price per unit less variable cost per unit — R95 less R48 gives R47

questions.question: Contribution is NOT profit because:
options: It must first pay toward the pile of fixed costs — only after they are covered does it fall through as profit
It is calculated before variable costs

questions.question: Total contribution at 24 000 pairs is:
The four-line factory income statement runs:
options: Sales, less fixed costs, contribution, less variable costs, profit
Sales, less cost of sales, gross profit, net profit
Sales, less variable costs, contribution, less fixed costs, profit

questions.question: The break-even formula in words is:
options: Total fixed costs divided by contribution per unit
Total costs divided by selling price
Fixed costs divided by selling price

questions.question: Kagiso's break-even point is:
options: 14 000 pairs — R658 000 over R47 — with a break-even value of R1 330 000

questions.question: Interpreted against planned production of 24 000 pairs, break-even at 14 000 means:
options: The survival line sits at 58,3 percent of the plan — a healthy cushion, with 10 000 pairs earning pure profit

questions.question: If the division gives 14 002 comma 1 units, the break-even point is:
options: 14 003 units — always round UP, because at 14 002 a sliver of loss remains

questions.question: The margin of safety on the budget is:
options: 10 000 pairs — 41,7 percent of planned sales can be lost before the loss line

questions.question: Cutting the price to R89 moves break-even to:
options: 16 049 pairs — a R6 cut attacks contribution directly and moves the line violently

questions.question: Fixed costs rising by R47 000 moves break-even to:
options: Exactly 15 000 pairs — R705 000 over the unchanged R47

questions.question: The break-even model assumes:
options: Fixed costs change with every unit
Constant price and unit variable cost, fixed costs that never step, and that everything made is sold

questions.question: The R658 pile of stones stands for:
options: The fixed costs — spent before roll one, the same whether you sell nothing or a mountain

questions.question: The R48 that travels with every roll is:
options: The variable cost per unit — wors, bread, sauce, serviette

questions.question: Each roll sold at R95 lifts how much off the pile?
options: R47 — the contribution: one stone per roll

questions.question: Busy sellers win twice because:
options: More contributions arrive AND the fixed cost per unit thins as volume spreads it

questions.question: With a pile of R658 and R47 lifted per roll, the pile is gone at:
options: Roll fourteen — and roll fifteen is the first sold purely for yourself

questions.question: If the division gives fourteen comma two rolls, you break even on:
options: Roll fifteen — round the survival line UP; at fourteen you are still one stone short

questions.question: Expecting to sell fifteen rolls with break-even at fourteen means:
options: One bad hour from a loss — the line only means something next to what you expect to sell

questions.question: The factory's version of roll fourteen is:

subtopics.title: When the Price of Wors Goes Up

questions.question: Wors up R3 a roll changes the survival line by:
options: Contribution drops to R44, so the line moves from fourteen to fifteen rolls
Nothing — wors is a fixed cost
The price must rise to R98

questions.question: A R6 discount on a R95 roll feels small but:
options: It only matters for big orders
It takes nearly thirteen percent of the contribution — price cuts bite the contribution, not the price
It changes nothing below ten percent

questions.question: A fixed-cost rise and a variable-cost rise move the line by different routes:
options: One grows the pile to be buried; the other shrinks every unit's stone-lifting power

questions.question: Break-even analysis is called a headlight because:
options: It prices decisions BEFORE they are made — leather, contracts and rent are tested before anyone signs
